title: Skip the Codex app-server probe when there are no credentials
head: 7b2bbd8b271c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A non-UTF-8 or unreadable Codex config aborts the entire collector before JSON is printed
leads.consequence: The new unconditional read_text() is outside both exception handlers and happens even if auth.json exists or CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN is set. A UnicodeDecodeError or PermissionError exits nonzero, so omarchy-agent-usage-update does not replace codex.json. The panel retains the previous record (or has none), losing even usable local usage counts. It affects normal and --limits-only runs.

leads.summary: Valid TOML single-quoted keyring or auto store is silently interpreted as file
leads.consequence: For cli_auth_credentials_store = 'keyring' (or 'auto'), with credentials stored only in the keyring and no auth.json/token, the line regex does not match. The collector emits empty limits plus login advice without probing, even though Codex accepts the configured store and could return meters. Quoted TOML keys and a value on a separate multiline TOML string likewise are not handled. Parsing a line is not equivalent to Codex's TOML deserialization.

leads.summary: A managed credential-store requirement can override config.toml, but the gate cannot see it
leads.consequence: If effective requirements.toml sets cli_auth_credentials_store = 'keyring' while user config is absent/file and credentials are only in the keyring, the gate skips usable rate limits. Reverse direction, a managed file requirement with user config keyring and no auth.json, still spawns the app-server. Codex prioritizes requirements over the ordinary TOML field; the collector reads only the latter.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2, source); corroboration

leads.summary: Open PR #13109 and #13102 add Codex-probe tests that fail after merging this auth gate
leads.consequence: #13109's LAUNCH_HOME installed-binary case and LINK_HOME symlink case assert that codex-args exists, but neither fixture creates auth.json, sets keyring/auto or passes CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN. #13102's CHUNKED_HOME fixture similarly has no credentials and asserts an RPC result. With this PR's gate merged, none spawns the stub, so these tests fail irrespective of merge order unless their new fixtures gain synthetic credentials. #12803's fixture also lacks auth but asserts only local scan outputs, so it does not fail for this reason.
leads.triage: #13109 already in Opus N3; #13102 factual, verified by coordinator patch read (coord/pr-13102-files.json), then confirmed by Opus run 20260927T064738Z-f77edabc; published

leads.summary: The parser also treats a setting under an unrelated TOML table as a top-level store
leads.consequence: A legitimate [mcp_servers.demo.env] cli_auth_credentials_store = 'keyring' sets an MCP environment variable, not the CLI auth store. With the same key using double quotes, the regex matches it as the store, spawns the app-server despite having no CLI credentials, and can reintroduce plugin fetch on each refresh. This is a narrower configuration collision than H2; an actual top-level setting should be scoped to its table.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2 table-key false positive, run with projects table); corroboration; MCP env example not used

leads.summary: On a fresh machine with no usage, the no-credentials record and login hint are invisible in the agents panel
leads.consequence: No sessions and no credentials yields no limits and zero usage, so providerHasData returns false even though the collector emits usageStatusText and authHelpText. The tab is filtered out, so a new user never sees the advertised login guidance in the panel. This visibility rule predates this PR; it is a limit of the intended no-credentials UX rather than a regression caused by this patch.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing panel visibility rule, not changed by this PR, out of follow-up scope

limits: Source-only boundary hunt, no PR code, live Codex binary, keyring, fixture or full test suite executed. Repo source and open PR file patches fetched read-only at the pinned head. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13106#issuecomment-5825278185), checked at `7b2bbd8b`. The [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13106#issuecomment-5825678463) describes the changes.

**Verified:** All three earlier points are resolved.

New in this round: the new `config.toml` read can crash the collector, the parser misses some store settings, and two open PRs have tests that will need an `auth.json` fixture.

| Earlier point | Status at `7b2bbd8b` |
|---|---|
| Keyring/auto store and `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` users lose their rate limits | Resolved |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`CODEX_API_KEY` exceptions keep the app-server spawn | Resolved |
| Optional test improvement: the no-credentials test inherits API-key variables | Resolved |

Collector runs with a stub `codex` that answers as logged in, `--limits-only`, no `auth.json`:

| Case | Previous head `bfbba368` | This head |
|---|---|---|
| `cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"` or `"auto"` | skip, no limits | probe, 2 limits |
| `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` set | skip, no limits | probe, 2 limits |
| only `OPENAI_API_KEY` or only `CODEX_API_KEY` set | probe | skip, "Codex limits unavailable" |
| no config, no token | skip | skip, "Codex limits unavailable" |

The earlier source claims still hold at the latest Codex release, `rust-v0.157.1`. The app-server still disables the environment API key, and saving to the keyring still deletes `auth.json`. The head test file passes 25/25, including with all three variables exported. Each new case fails against a collector variant that lacks the behaviour it tests.

**Documentation:** The PR description still lists `CODEX_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` as logins, which no longer matches the code after `7b2bbd8b`. Updating the description to drop them would keep it accurate.

### An unreadable or non-UTF-8 `config.toml` crashes the collector

`config_toml.read_text()` at [`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex:539`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/7b2bbd8b271c57a8375a5cd193807465d53ffd01/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex#L539) has no error handling and no explicit encoding, and no caller catches the exception. It runs whenever `codex` is on PATH and `config.toml` exists, even when `auth.json` exists.

| `config.toml` (`auth.json` present) | Base and `bfbba368` | This head |
|---|---|---|
| mode 000 | exit 0, full record | exit 1, `PermissionError`, empty stdout |
| contains byte `0xE9` (`LANG=C.UTF-8`) | exit 0, full record | exit 1, `UnicodeDecodeError`, empty stdout |

The mode 000 case fails the same way in full-scan mode.

**Impact:** `omarchy-agent-usage-update` treats the missing JSON as "codex collector failed" and keeps the previous `codex.json`. On a first run it writes none. The Codex tab then stops updating entirely, local token stats included, where base and `bfbba368` still printed a full record. Such a file is unlikely, but the failure is out of proportion to it.

**Suggested change:** Guard the read and fall through to the probe on any error other than a missing file. A variant that opens the file in binary mode, parses it with `tomllib` and probes on any exception passed the head test file (25/25) and fixed these cases. It also fixed the three syntax cases below (single-quoted value, quoted key, key inside a table). That variant was written during the review; it is not from the PR.

### The line regex misses some ways of setting the store

The regex only matches a double-quoted value with a bare key, in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` only.

- **Logged-in users treated as logged out** (the earlier finding, in narrower configurations):
  - Confirmed by run: `cli_auth_credentials_store = 'keyring'`, a valid TOML literal string that Codex's own test fixtures use, and a quoted key (`"cli_auth_credentials_store" = "keyring"`).
  - From source only: a store set in `/etc/codex/config.toml` when the user file does not set it, or enforced by `/etc/codex/requirements.toml` (or the legacy `/etc/codex/managed_config.toml`). Both apply at `rust-v0.156.1` and `rust-v0.157.1`, and a requirement overrides the user setting.
- **Probe still runs without a Codex login** (same as base, so not a regression, but the plugin sync stays):
  - Confirmed by run: the key inside a TOML table, for example after a `[projects."..."]` header. Codex does not read that as the top-level setting.
  - `"ephemeral"`: the collector probes (run), and by source a fresh app-server has no login under that store.

**Impact:** The first group loses the 5-hour and weekly meters and is told to run `codex login`. The second group keeps the refresh-time plugin sync the PR aims to remove. Both groups need unusual configurations.

**Suggested change:** Parse the file with `tomllib` and read only the top-level key, as in the variant above. Optionally, also read `/etc/codex/config.toml` when the user file does not set the key, and fall through to the probe when `/etc/codex/requirements.toml` or `/etc/codex/managed_config.toml` exists.

**Optional test improvement:** No test covers `auto`, and none sets only `CODEX_API_KEY`. A collector variant that checks `== "keyring"` in place of `!= "file"` passes the current tests, and so does one that re-adds the `CODEX_API_KEY` exception.

### Interaction with open PRs #13109 and #13102

Both PRs append tests whose fixtures have no `auth.json` and expect the collector to probe `codex`:

- **#13109** (`LAUNCH_HOME` and `LINK_HOME`). Combined with this head, "Codex collector probes the binary mise which reports" fails (confirmed by run). With `.codex/auth.json` added to those two fixtures, all 29 cases pass.
- **#13102** (`CHUNKED_HOME`). Combined with this head, "Codex collector reads a reply chunked together with a notification" fails (confirmed by run). With `.codex/auth.json` added to that fixture, all 26 cases pass.

In each pair, whichever PR lands second needs one `auth.json` line per affected fixture. #13109 and #13102 both append their tests at the same point in the test file, so their merges will also conflict textually.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Fresh follow-up review of head `7b2bbd8b` against `bfbba368` and the base. Sources read: this PR's code and tests, and the Codex CLI source at `rust-v0.156.1` and `rust-v0.157.1`. Sandboxed runs with no network: the scanner test files, a collector matrix and per-case variant runs against a stub `codex` whose replies are synthetic, and this head combined with #13109 and with #13102. Not tested: a live Codex binary, a real keyring or login, a network audit, and the `/etc/codex` and requirements layers.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
